Character Index - M[]

M'Lee[]

Appearances: Daredevil #213

M'Lee was a member of the Kinjorge tribe. After Micah Synn had forced Debbie Nelson to clean the floor of his penthouse, Debbie begged M'Lee to talk with her. She feigned interest but then poured water on her head as a cruel prank.[1]

Ma[]

Appearances: Marvel Zombies Supreme #2

Ma was an elderly Kansas resident and the wife of Pa. While returning home with her husband through the countryside, she witnessed a flaming object crash into a nearby field. The couple approached the impact site and discovered an unidentified being, asking whether it was injured. The creature was in fact the zombified Hyperion. After it attacked and devoured Pa, Ma attempted to hide beneath their pickup truck, but Hyperion eventually found and devoured her as well.[2]

Mabel[]

Appearances: Fantastic Four #18

Mabel and Zelda stumbled across the Fantastic Four while shopping in a New York department store.[3]

Mentioned: Daredevil #59

Mabel was having a telephone conversation with a friend, who suddenly reported Daredevil swinging past her telephone booth after foiling a pair of extortionists.[4]

Mac[]

Appearances: Tales of Suspense #38

A man who witnessed the social consequences of Bill Turner's wish that made everyone on Earth wealthy. While speaking with a police officer who announced his resignation due to his newfound riches, Mac reacted with disbelief, pointing out that society still needed police protection. His astonishment grew when another officer also declared he was quitting his job to enjoy his wealth.[5]

Appearances: Daredevil #58

Mac was a journalist who was trying to convince a court guard to allow him to take pictures at the trial against Mr. Big of the Underworld by not getting permission as the judge did not allow any cameras in the courtroom.[6]

Appearances: Avengers #155

Jones and Mac were two oceanographers who worked at the U.S. Government Oceanographic Research Center where they developed devices to be used on the sea floor. When they were testing one of these devices they were attacked by Attuma and his men, they initially managed to escape but later only the intervention of Beast and his allies prevented them and their collaborators from being killed.[7]

Appearances: Marvel Two-In-One #43

Mac was the lover and co-worker of Jo. While the two were together in the Everglades swamps, they encountered Jude the Entropic Man, who chose them as the first sacrifices to his creed of entropy. Using his destructive powers, Jude reduced both Mac and Jo to ashes.[8]

MacAllister[]

Appearances: Excalibur (Vol. 4) #20

Mrs. MacAllister was the mother of Alice (later Malice). After an argument with her daughter trying to make her understand that her behavior would only lead to unhappiness, she tried to make peace with her daughter but entering her room she found only the lifeless body of Alice, not knowing that her mutation had transformed her into a being of pure psychic energy.[9]

Macallister[]

Appearances: X-Factor (Vol. 3) #239

Liam Macallister's mother was killed by the goddess Morrigan with a sonic scream, like other members of the Macallister family.[10]

Macchio[]

Appearances: New Mutants Annual #3

The tennis player Macchio was meeting the tennis champion Ivan Lendl on the Wimbledon court when the match was interrupted by the arrival on the court of Impossible Man and Warlock to continue their challenge, putting the two tennis players to flight and taking their place.[11]

MacGruder[]

Appearances: Amazing Spider-Man (Vol. 2) #546

MacGruder was a shareholder of the Daily Bugle. During the newspaper's financial crisis, J. Jonah Jameson attempted to negotiate with MacGruder in an effort to maintain control of the company. However, MacGruder informed him that he had already sold his shares to Dexter Bennett.[12]

Mack[]

Appearances: Amazing Spider-Man #65

Mack and Rock Gimpy were the first two prisoners to be knocked out by Spider-Man during the escape attempt.[13]

Appearances: Deadpool (Vol. 2) #1

Mack was a scientist who worked with Dr. Langkowski at the Project Michelangelo facility in Antarctica.[14]

MacMillan[]

Appearances: Thunderbolts (Vol. 2) #168

MacMillan was an employee of Lloyd's of London. He went to the Raft to deliver to the Thunderbolts a chest held in a London bank since 1888, delivered by Ghost traveling through time and with instructions on where, when, and to whom to deliver it.[15]

MacMurphy[]

Appearances: X-Factor #88

Policeman MacMurphy noticed that his gun (and the guns of the other police he was with) had just rusted away, due to Prodigal's mutant power.[16]

MacMurray[]

Appearances: Alpha Flight #14

Inspector MacMurray questioned Puck about an incident in Lake Ontario near Ontario Place involving the disappearance of an infant in the Lake and the injury of Heather Hudson. MacMurray later told Puck that there were 16 victims missing in the Lake and the grisly account of the remains of those they had recovered.[17]

MacPherran[]

Appearances: She-Hulk #10, Fear Itself: The Worthy #3

Titania's father, seeing his newborn daughter declared that she was a small and weak thing without much struggle in her,[18] and also wondered how many double shifts he would have to do to support her too.[19]

Appearances: She-Hulk #10, Fear Itself: The Worthy #3

To her husband's negative comment about her newborn daughter's frailty, Titania's mother replied that her life would harden her...or so she believed.[18] Growing up, Mary's mother had to ignore her baby's requests because of her work.[19]

MacRae[]

Appearances: Doctor Strange (Vol. 2) #68

Doctor MacRae was a veterinarian hired by Dane Whitman to treat Valinor. MacRae was unaccustomed to treating creatures of a magical nature and infuriated Whitman at his inability to effectively help. Doctor Strange arrived and removed the enchantment that gave Valinor his wings since it was making him ill.[20]

MacReedy[]

Appearances: Wolverine: Switchback #1

MacReedy was the sadistic and psychopathic sheriff of Pottsville who killed only for the sake of killing the passers-by, until he met Logan and he was killed.[21]

Mad Dog[]

Appearances: Daredevil #295

Mad Dog was one of Daredevil's informants.[22]

Madeline[]

Appearances: Amazing Spider-Man #265

Madeline offered a towel to Silver Sable after her combat workout with members of the Wild Bunch at the Symkarian Embassy.[23]

Appearances: Elektra #2

Madeline interviewed Father Peter Nova.[24]

Appearances: Deadpool (Vol. 3) #40

Madeline was the secretary of Warden Aimes at Crossmoor Prison who could not stop Dr. Whitby from breaking into the Warden office during a meeting with Director-General Swinton.[25]

Maddy[]

Appearances: Hawkeye (Vol. 2) #2

Maddy was a Native American who lived on the Dunroman Reservation. She took her son to Dr. Avery to be treated for a broken arm he suffered playing hockey. She too, like the entire village, was killed by the Secret Empire when it razed the village to erase traces of their presence there.[26]

Maggie[]

Appearances: Lethal Foes of Spider-Man #1

Maggie was a prison guard on Ryker's Island, who greeted Leila Davis when she was released from prison and wished her that she would remain legit, as indeed she was before all the crazy things that had happened to her.[27]

Magistrate[]

Appearances: Incredible Hulk #304

The Magistrate was the leader of an alien species that confronted Zgorian on Zgorian's World after the arrival of the Hulk. Zgorian had been exiled to the world by his people but the Magistrate had arrived to execute the escalation of the sentence from exile to death and carried it out on Zgorian.[28]

Magliano[]

Mentioned: Amazing Spider-Man (Vol. 2) #666

Magliano was a boss in clandestine betting. He sent two of his henchmen against Leonard Kornfeld to punish him for not repaying his debts, but Leonard was bitten by the Jackal's mutated bedbugs which infected him with the Spider-Virus and taught Magliano's henchmen a stern lesson.[29]

Magon[]

Mentioned: Punisher Annual #4

A major New York drug dealer targeted by Punisher. After storming Magon's establishment and eliminating his men, the Punisher defeated him and forced him to reveal who was taking over the heroin market before killing him with a gunshot.[30]

Makoto[]

Mentioned: Punisher (Vol. 8) #15

Makoto was a member of the Hunter of Monster Special Force. Another Hunter member confided that perhaps he wasn't worthy of serving Hellsgaard because while they were hunting the Unseen Family, he failed to detect Brother Unseen, who nearly killed Hunter Makoto.[31]

Mal[]

Mentioned: Avengers #113

Mal was a member of the racist terrorist group the Living Bombs. After the Vision was seriously injured by one of the terrorist group, the others decided to finish the job by attacking the Stark Industries facility where they were trying to repair the Vision. Mal blew himself up while being thwarted by Captain America, but the explosion did no damage thanks to Scarlet Witch.[32]

Mallen[]

Appearances: Invincible Iron Man #3

Mallen's father was a smuggler and arms dealer. When the federals tried to chase them away from their property, he and his family armed themselves to oppose them, but they were all shot down by the federals before the eyes of his youngest son, the only survivor.[33]

Appearances: Invincible Iron Man #3

Mallen's older brother was killed along with the rest of his family by the federals when they tried to chase them away from their property and they in turn armed themselves to resist them, all this before the young Mallen's eyes.[33]

Mallory[]

Appearances: Daredevil #63

Dr. Mallory was a psychiatrist who worked in a prison and treated Melvin Potter who accused amnesia by saying that he was not the Gladiator and that he was framed. He then summoned Foggy Nelson and Matt Murdock for the acknowledgment that they confirmed that he was Potter.[34]

Mandy[]

Appearances: Ghost Rider (Vol. 6) #14

Mandy was Darlene's younger sister.[35]

Manfred[]

Appearances: Web of Spider-Man #24

Magnificent Manfred was a stage magician who performed at a casino in Atlantic City. During one of his shows, he brought Peter Parker on stage for a magic trick, in which Peter would be transported from one box to another, but when Manfred uncovered the two boxes, Peter was not in either of them, leaving Manfred stunned.[36]

Manito[]

Appearances: Daredevil: Reborn #3

Manito was a Cartels henchman to whom Calavera ordered that if Sheriff Cole had still spoken he would have to shoot him in the head.[37]

Mann[]

Appearances: Thunderstrike (Vol. 2) #3

Adam Mann's single mother, when his son was young, filled his head with the stories of the mythological characters and their adventures.[38]

Manning[]

Appearances: Journey Into Mystery #36

Manning was a colleague of Martin Henslowe, who, when Henslowe decided to demonstrate his discovery in being able to make animals talk, said that he admired his courage in carrying on his research, even though after the demonstration Henslowe was kicked out of the University. Twenty years later, when Manning had become head of the biology department, he met Henslowe again at the University who was unable to show him that he had managed to make a spider talk because as soon as he opened the box where the spider was, a janitor who was there, at the sight of the spider, squashed it with a broom.[39]

Appearances: U.S.Agent (Vol. 2) #5

The son of the tycoon April Manning was killed by policemen after being stopped driving his father's luxury car which made the policemen suspicious as this car was in the hands of a black boy.[40]

Manny[]

Appearances: Howard the Duck #29

Manny was the agent of Joey Goniff, a showman, who was fired by his client after he got bored of the various cheap shows Manny had given him in Cleveland.[41]

Appearances: Amazing Spider-Man #195

Manny used to watch Aunt May playing chess with Henry at the Restwell Nursing Home.[42]

Appearances: Peter Parker, The Spectacular Spider-Man #43, Peter Parker, The Spectacular Spider-Man #47, Peter Parker, The Spectacular Spider-Man #48

Manny, Jack, and Moe were Belladonna's henchmen. They participated in the various raids which, disguised as fashion design thefts, were put in place to discredit and ruin Roderick Kingsley.[43][44]
After tricking Spider-Man into going to Roderick Kingsley, Belladonna called Jack by phone telling him to get the boys together as that would be the big payoff. During the final showdown between Belladonna and her gang against Spider-Man, they were all easily defeated by the hero and handed over to the police.[45]

Appearances: Solo Avengers #1

Manny was a clown who was supposed to perform with Hawkeye for a charity show at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, but while he and the other clowns were getting ready in the dressing room they were hit by a soporific arrow from Trickshot who after falling asleep were replaced by a gang of murderous mercenaries.[46]

Appearances: Punisher (Vol. 2) #57

A member of Derek Pike's gang who assisted in the breakout that allowed Punisher to escape Ryker's Island in Pike's place, unaware of the switch due to the bandages covering Castle's face. After bringing him to a Brooklyn hideout, one of the gang members discovered that the man beneath the bandages was not Pike and called for Manny. Castle fought the two men and managed to escape.[47]

Appearances: Blood and Glory #2

Manny was a member of the Medisuelan National Defense Force under the Navatilas regime, answering to Colonel Antonio Veneno. Manny and Veneno were involved in operations related to illegal drug smuggling, with Navatilas' blessing, in a camp in Medisuelan jungles.[48]

Captain America investigated their operation, only to be caught in an explosion. Veneno and Manny found Captain America, unconscious. Manny jokingly said they had found Uncle Sam due to the colorful costume; Veneno had Manny shut up and contact Navatilas.[48]

Navatilas' forces then attacked the camp in an attempt to remove any loose ends. The stray bullets probably killed Manny.[49]

In Blood and Glory #1, two Medisuelans named Carlos and Manuel "Manny" are involved in a weapon smuggling operation in American soil; both are killed, so neither of them is this person. The names Carlos and Manny are swapped during the scene (One of the men has a moustache, the other one is shaven, but both are named "Manny" and "Carlos" at some point).

Appearances: Marvel Team-Up #136

A researcher at Steyr Security Systems, Manny removed Spider-Man's webbing with his portable laser torch.[50]

Appearances: Daredevil #304

The stroller with Manny in it got stuck between the automatic doors of the subway and at the end of the platform he was catapulted into the void and only the intervention of Daredevil who catch him on the fly made sure he was saved and was delivered safely to his parents.[51]

Appearances: Amazing Spider-Man #395

Manny was a drug dealer working under Mr. White. Like his boss, he was confronted and defeated by Nocturne and Puma.[52]

Appearances: Ghost Rider (Vol. 3) #70

Manny was Happy Jack Karne's bodyguard and when the Ghost Rider assaulted his boss he bravely came between them shouting that he wasn't afraid of him but the Ghost Rider easily overwhelmed him and killed him.[53]

Appearances: Captain Marvel (Vol. 4) #26

Manny was a petty thief and a homeless man who found a faint Rick Jones on the pavement, who had a bracelet on him, not knowing that it was actually a Nega-Band. Manny took it from Rick and sold it to a pawnshop who offered him a lot of money, but immediately after that bargaining Manny had a crisis of conscience for having stolen something from someone he thought was a poor homeless person and also thought about the reaction his partner Deb would have, then he returned to the pawn shop and had the bracelet returned, giving back the money. He later discovered that the old homeless man had helped Deb give birth and that he had saved their child and then Manny gave him back the bracelet.[54]

Appearances: Savage Wolverine #16

Manny was a henchman of Marion who was killed in a gunfight in the prison where Logan was being held.[55]

Appearances: Runaways (Vol. 5) #33

Manny was a student at Griffith Park High School who got acquainted with his classmate Gert Yorkes during a school shooting drill. He later ran into her while making his way through the bleachers during a school football game.[56] He later partnered with Gert for a group project.[57]

Manoel[]

Appearances: Marvel's Voices: Community #1

When Shark Girl went to Brazil to buy some typical dishes of her country, Manoel, after the fright he had at seeing Iara come out of the water with his shark aspect, calmed down and having learned of Iara's intentions he took her to his father who owned a kiosk where he sold traditional Brazilian food.[58]

Manuel[]

Appearances: Avengers #31

Manuel was one of the policemen who met the Avengers, when they were looking for Goliath and Dr. Anton.[59]

Appearances: X-Men #26

Manuel was a policeman controlled by Kukulcàn.[60]

Appearances: Marvel Team-Up #114

Manuel, a member of the Young Watchers vigilante group of Harlem, was a friend of Jim Wilson.[61]

Appearances: Marvel Team-Up #119

Manuel was a member of a gang of thugs who were stopped by Spider-Man and the Gargoyle as they attempted to assault an old lady. After being caught and left webbed, the police did not show up and when the web dissolved they fled and then attacked Nathan Lubensky at the Theatre District and were once again stopped and captured by Spider-Man.[62]

Appearances: Web of Scarlet Spider #3

Manuel was grabbed by the Scarlet Spider and stranded on the railing of the observation deck of the Empire State Building.[63]

Manuelo[]

Appearances: Uncanny X-Men #438

Manuelo was a member of Jay Guthrie's band in Kentucky. He was present when Julia walked into the locker room and realised Jay's wings were real.[64]

Mara[]

Appearances: Web of Scarlet Spider #3

Mara witnessed the Scarlet Spider grab Manuel and strand him on the railing of the observation deck of the Empire State Building.[63]

Appearances: Amazing Spider-Man: You're Hired! #1

Mara is an employee of the municipality of New York who explains through the Forceworks1 project the functioning of the "Made in NY" program.[65]

Marc[]

Appearances: Untold Tales of Spider-Man #1

Marc was a henchman for Scorcher. During their last heist at a Chemical Warehouse, Marc complained to Scorcher that they were surrounded by the police, but Scorcher reassured him that everything was going according to plan.[66]

Marcel[]

Appearances: Marvel Comics Presents #68

Marcel was an antiquity seller from Paris.[67]

Marcellino[]

Appearances: Venom (Vol. 2) #1

Marcellino was a member of the armored United Nations Peacekeeping Forces stationed in the nation of Nrosvekistan. He was killed in the clash with Jack O'Lantern.[68]

Marcia[]

Appearances: Spider-Man #80

Marcia lived in a building attacked by Crown and Hydra.[69]

Appearances: Fantastic Four (Vol. 3) #517

Marcia was an adviser to the mayor of New York City. During a crisis, she insisted on refusing to ask for help from the Fantastic Four to the point where the mayor refused to listen to her advice and fired her.[70]

Marco[]

Appearances: Ms. Marvel (Vol. 4) #8, Ms. Marvel (Vol. 4) #9, Ms. Marvel (Vol. 4) #10, Ms. Marvel (Vol. 4) #11

Marco was one of the volunteers who were put together in the Carol Cadets by Becky St. Jude to put Ulysses' knowledge to good use.[71]

Appearances: Taskmaster (Vol. 3) #2

Marco was the owner of a comic shop in Washington D.C. where Phil Coulson used to go to buy his favorite comics.[72]

Appearances: Carnage: Black, White & Blood #3

Marco was a member of the heavy metal band Brain Flayer who was killed in the Carnage massacre of the Magpie Club which killed all the band members except Blake Bellman.[73]

Marcus[]

Mentions: Giant-Size Man-Thing #2

Marcus was a member of Dr. Dane Gavin's expedition team during the effort to capture the Man-Thing in the Florida Everglades. Present when Gavin's electrically powered trap successfully weakened and restrained the creature, Marcus became nervous when Gavin ordered the electrical current shut off, questioning whether it was truly safe to deactivate the system while the Man-Thing was still inside the containment area.[74]

Mentions: Amazing Spider-Man #225

Miss Marcus was a figure associated with Empire State University who was referenced by employees of the mailroom. During a moment of idleness, while workers were playing cards instead of performing their duties, one employee—apparently speaking with authority over the others—amused himself by recounting how he had sarcastically replied to Miss Marcus that he did not allow “his boys” to gamble on the job.[75]

Mentions: Astonishing X-Men (Vol. 3) #49

Marcus was Susan Hatchi 's driver. Susan instructed her assistant to call Marcus and have him drive her car around.[76]

Appearances: Daredevil (Vol. 6) #26, Daredevil (Vol. 6) #27, Daredevil (Vol. 6) #28, Daredevil (Vol. 6) #29

Marcus was a prisoner in the same prison where Daredevil had been incarcerated. He disagreed with Daredevil's right to keep his mask on and believed that this privilege was indicative that he would not be in prison for the time he was sentenced.[77]
During the onslaught of Knull's symbiotes, Marcus helped Daredevil get rid of his symbiote by giving him a jolt in the electric chair.[78]
Daredevil thanked Marcus for helping him, and the two had lunch together, but Daredevil realized he had been poisoned.[79] After telling Marcus, Daredevil left calmly trying to get outdoors.[80]

Marcy[]

Appearances: Marvel Two-In-One #86

Marcy was Flint Marko's girlfriend around the time he started crime. When he was first imprisoned, Marcy began a secret relationship with a member of Marko's gang, and when he got out of prison earlier than expected he caught them together by teaching Marcy's lover a stern lesson and she herself was scared of him, and their relationship ended.[81]

Appearances: Wolverine (Vol. 6) #1, Wolverine (Vol. 6) #5

Marcy is one of the members of The Offer's squad. She works as The Offer's computers expert and monitors the activities of the field team.[82]

With her subordinates Roberta, Sheila, and Sophia, she was involved in the murders of several political hopefuls who had voted for an increase in spending for better police protection. Silver Sable and Chen, by then Sable's employee, investigated the murders and Sable killed Sophia. Chen then infiltrated in the guild; Maria sent Chen to murder a Maggioso as a test, and Chen pretended to comply, but Maria discovered how Chen was trying to trick them, and arranged a trap for her, pretending to accept her in a heist with them to kill Maggia Don Alfredo Magnano and his associates in his Long Island villa. Silver Sable found out the murder they were planning through her contact the Foreigner. In the villa, when Chen refused to kill in cold blood, Maria revealed that it was a trap for Chen; Roberta and Sheila killed several of the Maggiosi there, and Chen tried to escape through the villa's garden. The guild chased after her, but Sable joined her and defeated Sheila, then Roberta, and saved Chen from Maria. Aghast at hearing Chen call Sable "M'lady", Maria taunted Chen to see if Chen would kill her; Chen only knocked Maria down. Sable then cashed the bounties for the four assassins.[95]

Santera insisted on going to New York City for this, which led to the intervention of superheroes Ghost Rider, Venom, and Stigmata (a secret agent of the Catholic Church, supposedly working as the Santeras' bodyguard to verify that Santera had really converted), in turn leading to an escalating situation that Marta complained about, saying that she and the dwarves had played their role but Santera's plan had trainwrecked. The hostages were rescued, and Santera was arrested by the Vatican; the fate of Marta was not revealed.[137]

Matuscek[]

Appearances: Avengers (Vol. 3) #9

Matuscek is a woman working for superhuman criminal and weapons manufacturer Moses Magnum in the floating resort Evangeline in the Caribbean Sea. When Magnum's forces stole a seismic cannon in the John F. Kennedy International Airport and took it to the Evangeline so as to use to alter Magnum's uncontrolled superpowers, Matuscek was the operator of the cannon's controls while Magnum submitted to it. Magnum demanded that Matuscek gave him the readings and obeyed his instructions, even when she warned him they were going beyond any safety measure. The procedure was interrupted when the Avengers sneaked in and Magnum was forced to attack them, personally and with his guards; the cannon was damaged in the fight, and Matuscek probably had a chance to escape the battleground.[273]

Matuscek may be a member of Magnum's private army Magnum Shells, in active at that point, or an employee of Magnum's company Magnum Munitions, or an external contractor; her affiliation, besides obeying Magnum's commands, is not stated.

Maud[]

Mentions: Wolverine (Vol. 2) #119

Maud was the client of the assassin McLeish. During a conversation with Logan in a Hong Kong pub, McLeish recounted how he had once been hired by Maud to kill her husband. After completing the contract, McLeish returned to Maud carrying her husband's severed head. Maud complained that she had wanted the entire body, as otherwise she could not be certain that her husband was actually dead. Taking advantage of his skill as a ventriloquist, McLeish made the severed head appear to speak, pretending that her husband was asking Maud to marry him again and promising that he would never leave her. Convinced by the macabre performance, Maud offered McLeish an additional $50,000 to take the head away with him. McLeish used the anecdote to illustrate to Logan the peculiar difficulties that came with being a professional assassin.[274]

McMurdo[]

Appearances: Rampage (Vol. 2) #40, Rampage (Vol. 2) #42, Rampage (Vol. 2) #43, Rampage (Vol. 2) #44

McMurdo was studying the stars when the arrival of a craft from the future caused him to be engulfed by unknown energies. Tormented by strange visions, he soon encountered first the craft's occupant, a Time Traveler from the far future being pursued by mechanical killers, and then the mysterious Kilgore Slaughter, who had been given great powers by the same event. McMurdo's dog was killed by the Time Traveler's pursuers, but McMurdo himself survived and he and his daughter gave both the Time traveler and Slaughter sanctuary after helping Slaughter to destroy the corrupt future world the Traveler came from. McMurdo hoped to continue to use the killer Droids' time capsule to explore time itself, but it is unknown whether he ever achieved his objective.[320][321]

Melloncamp[]

Appearances: Marvel Tales (Vol. 2) #256

Dr. Melloncamp worked for the Deterrence Research Corporation. In such capacity, she repaired the alien Energy Synthecon that gave powers and linked DRC superhuman agents Hammer and Anvil when it was broken by Spider-Man.[348][349] She then tried to leave the company, but Hammer and Anvil were worried that their synthecon may break again, and decided to chase Melloncamp and keep her for her knowledge.[349] She had also developed a new procedure to keep Hammer and Anvil's symbiotic link functional, and they demanded that she use it.[350] She tried to escape from them by car, but crashed[349] when she swerved to avoid three circus performers (Gorilla Girl, Muck Monster, and Six). The Freaks pulled her from the burning vehicle, only for Hammer and Anvil to arrive and recapture Melloncamp. However, the three empathized with the doctor's plight and defeated Hammer and Anvil. She walked away with them.[349][350]


Chased by Hammer and Anvil, Melloncamp describes them as two escaped convicts. However, the story in Marvel Tales (Vol. 2) #256 takes place after Marvel Team-Up #86 (explicitly referencing that Melloncamp repaired the device when it was broken in Marvel Team-Up #86) and, per Official Handbook of the Marvel Universe Master Edition #27, Anvil profile, before Spider-Woman #34. At that point, Hammer and Anvil had been released from prison through legal means by the DRC, and they were not escaped convicts.

Mildred was a civilian caught in a near-accident while shopping with friends when a runaway bus crashed toward a store. She was saved by the timely intervention of Scarlet Witch and Wonder Man, with the latter stopping the vehicle at the cost of the storefront window. After the danger passed, Mildred reacted with excitement at meeting real superheroes and rushed to Scarlet Witch, asking for her autograph while largely ignoring Wonder Man's role in saving her.[439]

Appearances: Amazing Spider-Man #201

Mildred and her husband witnessed Spider-Man crashing into their apartment's window.[440]

Milo[]

Appearances: Iron Man (Vol. 3) #13

Appearances: Emma Frost #7, Emma Frost #8, Emma Frost #9, Emma Frost #10, Emma Frost #11, Emma Frost #12

Milo was a henchman of Lucien Goff who went to Troy Killkelly to force him into getting the loan with interest that Lucien had granted to Troy.[448]
Milo and Stu went again to visit Troy for payment with the intention of harming him again, but Emma had mentally sensed their arrival and together with Troy they managed to escape from the fire escape. However they managed to follow them to the restaurant where Troy worked but Emma used her powers to freeze both of them and Troy hit them with a frying pan, stunning them.[449]
Milo and Stu turned Troy's apartment upside down to get him to pay. Soon after they forced Troy and Emma to get into a car threatening them with guns.[450]
Stu and Milo disagreed about Emma's false kidnapping for a ransom, but they had to obey Lucien.[451]
Milo and Stu took care of making Troy's body disappear.[381]
Milo died in the shooting between various members of Lucien's gang after Emma had filled their minds with doubts and suspicions.[452]

Milty[]

Appearances: Uncanny Tales #41

Jasper Milty's son was not very happy that his elderly father decided to retreat to a cabin in the woods to get away from the progress and frenzy of the city, but he accepted it anyway. Later, he told his son Tom about the rush to buy Geiger counters to detect uranium, and Tom secretly got together with his boss and had a Geiger counter delivered to his grandfather in the woods. Much to the surprise of his relatives, Jasper actually discovered a deposit of uranium, thus making himself and his family wealthy.[455]

Appearances: Uncanny Tales #41

Jasper Milty's daughter-in-law was not very happy that her elderly father-in-law decided to retire to a cabin in the woods to get away from the progress and frenzy of the city, but she accepted it anyway thinking that he had done it so as not to burden his family. Later, her son Tom heard from her husband that there was a rush to buy Geiger counters to detect uranium, and Tom secretly made an agreement with her husband's boss and had a Geiger counter delivered to his father-in-law in the woods. Much to the surprise of his relatives, Jasper actually discovered a deposit of uranium, thus making himself and his family wealthy.[455]

Minton[]

Appearances: Mystery Men #3

When Dr. Rupert Kingsley dared to treat a member of the miners' union who had been beaten by his men, Minton in punishment set fire to Kingsley's house with him inside. The badly burned Kingsley became the vigilante Surgeon and his first action was to avenge of Minton torturing him before killing him by getting a lot of information on the Board.[462]

Moon Knight rushed to her rescue by defeating the Cult members in their secret lair and freeing Mirwit.[464]

Misty[]

Appearances: Amazing Spider-Man Annual #1996

Appearances: Deadpool (Vol. 2) #47

Misty was the daughter of the crime boss Big Eddie B. Using his Image Inducer, Deadpool approached Eddie while disguised as Mike the Monster, another prominent crime lord. In this false guise, Deadpool claimed that Eddie had betrayed him by having an affair with his wife and further alleged that he was now showing interest in Eddie's daughter, Misty, whom he claimed to have noticed outside her school. This elaborate deception was orchestrated with the sole purpose of turning the two criminal bosses against one another, manipulating their mutual distrust and rage until the conflict inevitably escalated, ultimately leading to both men destroying each other.[468]

Sensing the certain failure of his latest production, Silverberg told Mitchell to bring the script to his studio, seeing if he could at least turn the film into a comedy. Miyazaki[]

Appearances: Big Hero 6 #1

Principal Miyazaki was the head of the Teruka Advanced Science Institute, a Tokyo school attended only by a select few who had demonstrated exceptional intellectual abilities. While Hiro Takachiho and some of his classmates were chatting outside the building, Principal Miyazaki caught them off guard, reminding them that the bell was about to ring and they were expected to be in class. As Hiro's friends hurried inside, Miyazaki stopped Hiro, telling him he had noticed the presence of the two girls who had approached him earlier—actually his teammates Honey Lemon and Go‑Go Tomago—and asked whether there was a problem he could help with. Hiro thanked him and said he would take care of it.[479]

After Pepper's departure—prompted in part by Tony's offhand suggestion of a dinner arrangement delivered with his typical bravado—it was revealed that Monique had been concealed inside the same bathtub throughout the encounter, silently holding her breath to avoid detection.[503]

Murray[]

Appearances: Deadpool (Vol. 2) #45

Joe and Murray were two guards guarding "Titania" and Constrictor who had been captured by the Avengers. It was actually not Titania, but rather the shape-shifter Copycat who pretended to be a guard who had been captured by a supposedly escaped Titania and put there in her place. As soon as Joe and Murray opened the capsule that imprisoned him, she kicked them both out of action.[549]

Mushbell[]

Appearances: All Select Comics #11, Blonde Phantom Comics #12

Senator Mushbell was a United States senator during the 1940s. By 1946, he was providing government secrets to diplomat Signor Korte, the constant nemesis of the Blonde Phantom.[550][551]

Mushi[]

Appearances: Fear Itself: Spider-Man #3

Mushi was a nurse who assisted Dr. Shahrazad Rafiee at the E.R. of the General Hospital on the very day of the Fear Itself crisis with a large number of patients.[552]

Mushnik[]

Appearances: Secret Wars II #3

Mushnik was a drug smuggler who imported cocaine for the Beyonder when he was living in Manhattan and learning what it was like to be human.[553]

Mussorgsky[]

Appearances: Wolverine: Patch #5

Captain Mussorgsky took command of the Russian forces in Madripoor after Raskalnikov's death tasked with recapturing the mutant family who had fled Russia and bringing them back to their homeland.[554]

Muwhezi[]

Appearances: Muties #3

Mr. Muwhezi was a teacher in a school in the Gulu District of Uganda. He reprimanded his 13-year-old student Riek Bukenya for his mediocre results. When a team of soldiers raided the school to kidnap the students and take them to Sudan to train them as soldiers, they killed Muzewhi.[555]

Mycroft[]

Appearances: Iron Man #316

Mycroft used brain cybernetic implants to increase his intellect. He was hired by Roxxon to oppose Tony Stark's new ethical business policies.[556]

Myers[]

Appearances: Man-Thing #2

Dr. Myers was one of several scientists assembled by F.A. Schist to address the threat posed by the Man-Thing. After Schist presented footage of the creature and claimed it had murdered one of his workers, he offered a financial reward to anyone capable of killing it. Myers disagreed with Schist's interpretation of the events, having reviewed police reports indicating that the worker's death had effectively been caused by his own actions. Rather than destroying the Man-Thing, Myers believed the creature should be captured and scientifically studied.[557]

Appearances: Spider-Woman #26

Myers was a journalist who worked for the Los Angeles Courier for years and admired the paper's journalistic integrity. When the Courier was purchased by the Englishman Rupert Dockery, infamous for his sensationalist diaries, Myers and another like-minded journalist, Frederick, met with Dockery to express their concern about the Courier's possible drift. Dockery reassured them, falsely promising that the Courier would remain on its previous course, but as soon as the meeting was over, he contacted another employee, Dunlop, to fire Fredericks and Myers the next morning.[237]

Frederick and Myers appear in the same scene and it's unclear which of them is Myers. The bespectacled man was called Mike.

Myron[]

Appearances: Spectacular Spider-Man #134

Myron was a clerk in a jewelry store who was robbed by Maxwell Dillon. Myron smiled as Dillon pulled out a toy gun not imagining that Dillon would use his powers that electrocuted him and stunned him.[558]

Appearances: Ghost Rider (Vol. 3) #35

Myron was a former A.I.M. agent who was forced by Officer Badilino to a special weapon against the Ghost Rider.[559]

Appearances: Spider-Man #98

Myron witnessed Norman Osborn being taken away by the Scrier.[560]

Myrtle[]

Appearances: Sensational She-Hulk #13

Myrtle witnessed her grandson being crushed by the anomaly in Mount Pressure.[561]
